# tag: v0.7.1 (the latest release tag; annotated tag object d280afe09ebaf406dd954a37ac7d1f4314d93d14)
# commit: 066f86dbae867f00f5d0340a2ce6a83cbed2e088 (packaging: v0.7.1 release notes)
# built: the unmodified tag, from `git archive v0.7.1` extracted into a scratch directory, with the tag's own go.mod and go.sum (go directive 1.23.0). Only two things were added to it: this recorder (internal/source/mimecorpus_test.go, TestRecordMimeGoldens) and testdata/mime. Run as `go test ./internal/source -run '^TestRecordMimeGoldens$' -args -mime-record-dir=<dir> -mime-record-provenance=<file>`. No other file of the tag was changed.
# toolchain: go1.26.9 on darwin/arm64, the only toolchain available to the recording. The parts of the parser that the module shares with the toolchain (net/mail, mime, mime/quotedprintable, encoding/base64, the unicode tables) are therefore that toolchain's, not the release's: design OR4's residual, an open condition that S1's MA-331 closes by vendoring them.
# dependencies: github.com/emersion/go-message v0.16.0, github.com/emersion/go-mbox v1.0.4, github.com/mooijtech/go-pst/v6 v6.0.2, golang.org/x/text v0.21.0, golang.org/x/net v0.10.0, as the tag's go.mod and go.sum pin them
# recorded: 2026-10-11, by slice MF-S0 of docs/design-mime-fidelity.md, before any fidelity change
# same-as-branch: internal/source/ at the tag is byte-identical to the branch this slice is built on (fix/review-2026-10 at a26ec8a); internal/model/message.go differs only by added fields and FingerprintNoAttachments, which Identity, Fingerprint and ContentDigest do not read; the branch builds with x/text v0.42.0 and x/net v0.60.0, and TestMimeGoldensHoldForTheBuild shows it reproduces this file byte for byte
# body-fallback: BodyFallback (MC29) lands in internal/export after the tag; these goldens are parser-level, so it does not touch them
# content-fields: the content golden leaves out Locator, ReadGaps and ReadError, which the tag's model does not have; support.pst is somebody else's real mail, so its items are pinned by length and SHA-256 and their text is not copied here
# baseline: a baseline in the CLAUDE.md sense; regenerating it is an operator-accepted act under design section 5, never a fix
